newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to liberalise govt paper mkt for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Russia to liberalise govt paper mkt for foreigners.

text.p: Foreigners will soon have the same rights as domestic investors on Russia's government securities market, a senior finance ministry official said on Thursday.

"In two to three years non-residents will be able to enter the market in the same way as residents, but changing of course, their pounds and dollars into roubles," securities department head Bella Zlatkis told a conference on foreign investment.
A central bank official said the authorities could improve access to the market for foreigners by the end of 1997.
The International Monetary Fund has called on Russia to improve this access as part of its commitment to currency convertibility.

Since August non-residents have been able to open special rouble S-accounts at designated Russian banks. They can use roubles in these accounts to buy government securities at auction and trade them in the secondary market.
But they can only repatriate funds from the accounts through forward or option agreements with a term of at least three months.

The central bank requires commercial banks conducting these forward deals to offset 75 percent of them with the central bank at non-market rates set by the central bank -- allowing the authorities to influence the dollar return available to non-residents from investing in Russian government securities.
The authorities also control the total amount of money coming into the S-accounts each month.
The central bank said from the start that this system would be gradually liberalised.

Zlatkis said the central bank planned to eliminate the requirement to use forward deals, and in the meantime the central bank would reduce the proportion of offsetting deals which Russian commercial banks are required to conduct with it.
A steady rise in non-resident investment in the market has resulted in falling yields, and Zlatkis said she expected the yield on six-month paper to fall to 40-45 percent by the end of the year.
At the latest six-month paper auction on Wednesday the annualised average yield amounted to 58.46 percent.
